recipes.name: Chef John’s Peach Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 5 cups fresh peaches - peeled, pitted, and sliced

steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Combine peaches, Chinese five-spice powder, and lemon zest in a bowl.
Stir sugar and water together in saucepan pan over medium heat until simmering, 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in peach mixture; cook and stir for 2 minutes. Remove from heat and set aside.
Combine sugar and self-rising flour in a large bowl. Pour in milk; whisk to form a smooth batter.
Pour melted butter into a Dutch oven. Pour batter over the melted butter.
Gently place peaches and syrup on top of batter. As the cobbler bakes, they will sink down into the batter.
Bake until syrup is bubbling and crust has risen and is golden brown, about 50 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Chef John’s Peach Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This fabulous peach cobbler works just as well with canned peaches!

review.reviewBody:
This is an excellent recipe! To the reviewers who said that they had too much liquid after baking or that the crust never rose to the top, YOU USED THE WRONG TYPE OF FLOUR. This recipe calls for self-rising flour, NOT all-purpose, and there is a difference!
I made this as directed, subbing cinnamon for the 5-spice powder (I have simple tastes!) and it turned out wonderfully and was delicious!
A little trick for helping it to set better. After the bake time is over, turn the heat off and let the cobbler remain in the oven for a while to cool. This will let any remaining liquid boil off while not burning the dessert.
You should eat this warm though, rather than room temp. (Just my opinion!)
All in all, this is a great recipe. You can't go wrong with Chef John!

This is the second time I made this delicious peach cobbler. The first time I used my All Clad casserole thinking it was heavy enough. And I only used enough butter to coat the bottom of the pan. It turned out delicious but, like other reviews, the bottom was too doughy. This time I borrowed my son’s cast iron casserole and used the entire stick of butter. It turned out exactly as pictured. In fact, I was so proud that I took a picture and will see if I can figure out how to include it. After reading other reviews, I decided to cut back on the milk by 3/4 which didn’t seem to matter. And, my fresh peaches were so juicy, I skipped the simple syrup. Instead of adding 1 cup white sugar to the peaches, I used 1/4 cup brown sugar. And instead of 1 cup of sugar to the flour, I used 3/4 cup. I also added 1/2 tsp vanilla to the batter and the peaches.

A few notess to improve upon an already outstanding dish: 
DO NOT fail to use a DEEP pan. It will bubble over and you'll lose beautiful delish juices if you don't! Cinnamon is heavenly on peaches which DO NOT require simple syrup, IF they're summery-ripe and juicy. Use only 1/2cup sugar (1/4cup brown sugar+1/4cup granulated sugar) stirred with a dash of cinnamon over sliced peaches and allowed to sit 5-10 minutes while sugar melts as juices are drawn out. Melt the butter over heat in the same pan you'll bake it in, lightly browning. Browned butter flavor is divine! Proceed otherwise as Chef John directs. It may need 60-70 minutes to bake through before cooling just enough (at least 20 minutes) to experience cobbler-ecstasy!

Amazing! Added a cup of blueberries to the peaches in syrup while I waited for them to cool and the oven to heat. Used the convection at 350F, and it took barely 40 minutes to bake. Tested with a fine skewer to make sure the cake part was cooked. Also cut down the sugar in the batter to 1/2 cup. I divided this between a regular loaf pan and a smaller one. Unfortunately unable to upload photo. Because I had 4 cups of sliced peaches I cut back on the syrup, ie 3/4 cup of sugar and 3/4 cup of water. Will definitely make this again. Going to try a version using rhubarb which I will simmer for a few minutes in the simple syrup. Thank you chef John.

First time I made this, I thought the filling-topping ratio was a little off -- too much cake, not enough peaches. Year later, I've cut the flour-milk part by 2/3 and according to reviews, also altered the filling. What came out was amazing, with significantly less sugar, but more peach.
...
If you're interested, this is what I did (although I pretty much eye-balled the filling based on my tastes): 5 ripe peaches sliced into a large saucepan (actually it was more like a wok lol) + lemon juice, two cinnamon sticks, a sprinkle of cinnamon/nutmeg/anise, salt, 1/3 cup water, and enough sugar to cover the top, around 1/2 cup (since i'm not a big sweet tooth). Let it simmer on med for 5-8 minutes to reduce and strengthen the peachy-ness. As it simmers, add more sugar as needed. Brown sugar also works nicely.
*The cinnamon sticks were a really nice touch. If you have them, use! (of course take them out before adding to the batter)

I cut the butter to 1/4 cup, and decided to bake it in a cast iron pan. I didn't have self-rising flour so I tried substituting it with AP flour + baking powder, but it didn't work. It still turned out delicious though.

What a fast and easy cobbler to put together! I used home-grown home-canned peaches. Made this once with self rising flour in a Pyrex, and once with AP flour etc. in a dutch oven. Self-rising flour came out better, but both were very good. I think the sugar could be reduced some without making much a difference in flavor. Came out surprisingly similar to my Mom's biscuit-style cobbler.

This is, hands down, the best peach cobbler I’ve ever had! I’ve made it 5 times already. Based on other comments, I was worried that the amount of liquid would be too much. Each time I made the syrup and cooked the peaches (1lb 8 oz) it would yield 1-1/2 cups of liquid. The first few times, I just added half the liquid but found that the cobbler was not juicy enough. When I finally added the whole 1-1/2 cups, it took longer to bake (15 minutes or so more) but the peaches underneath had the perfect amount of syrup underneath the crust. To my liking, I have added 1/4 teas of cinnamon and a few rasps of whole nutmeg in place of the five spice, but even without those changes, this is a five star recipe.

I mistakenly thought I needed 3cups of peaches so I ended up making a smaller version. I used a deep 9in pie pan on top of a cookie sheet encase of overflow. I used cinnamon instead of 5-spice and I didn't use lemon zest at all. It took longer to bake than the recipe had said. I just kept checking it till the top was golden. Many people said that there was too much syrup so I set aside part of the syrup instead of adding it all. It turned out AMAZING!
You can make self-rising flour by adding1-1.5 tsp baking powder and 1/4salt to 1 cup of APF.

I used his basic recipe. I had just canned some peaches (using a lite syrup made with Truvia) and used about 1.3 quarts of the peaches, the syrup, and then added about a 2/3 pint of fresh blueberries. Added orange zest, cinnamon and some orange juice to the syrup, as well as about 1/2 cup of Splenda Brown Sugar. When I made the batter, I used Truvia again. After layering the butter and batter in the baking dish, I spooned over the peaches and blueberries and then cooked down the remaining syrup somewhat. Then spooned it over all of it. Baked at 350 as directed. And left it in the oven, with the oven 'off', for five more minutes. It is perfectly amazing !!! (I also added almond extract to the batter...)

This was my first time trying a peach cobbler and I am soooo glad I tried this recipe. It was AMAZING!! I read a lot of the reviews and I made a few changes: I used 1/2 tsp of cinnamon instead of the suggested seasoning, I baked it in my cast iron skillet and I didn’t use all of the juice when placing the peaches on top of the mixture. I think using the cast iron skillet allowed it make a nice crust on the outside. I will definitely be making this again.

Used 1/2 & 1/2 creamer, all purpose flour with baking powder & baking soda I cooked this on my gas grill 50min. On the side I turned off on the grill. 350 degrees fresh peaches unpeeled peel doesn't bother me. Delicious yum perfect!!

I've made this numerous times and it never fails. I love Chinese Five Spicy so I use it generously. I also throw in dried lemon peel and vanilla bean paste. For the batter I add dried lemon peel as well. I've also made it with berries. Like all of Chef John's recipes they are a keeper and if you love to bake and cook you know his recipes provide a great base for experimenting as well.

I didn't have self-rising flour, so I made my own by adding baking flour and salt. Worked fine. I also cut the recipe in half, since I'm the only one living here. My peaches weren't freestone, but they were tree-ripened from a farmer's market, so not only did they come off the pits easily, but I could peel the skin off with just my fingers. Win! Only half of the peaches sank, so I'm not sure why that happened. Still too hot to taste yet.
This cobbler turned out atrocious. It didn't set, didn't brown, and the bottom was absolute rubber. Inedible.
So far the recipe was a challenge, I like challenges! It’s in the oven so with fingers crossed 🤞🏼, it will be a masterpiece!
The peaches were at height of season. Juicy and sweet. Because of this, I cut the sugar and liquid of syrup in half. Also reduced the sugar in batter in half too. Sooo delicious! Will make again.
Didn't have Chinese spice, substituted cinnamon and nutmeg. Batter did not rise all the way, but was brown and tasty nonetheless. Self-rising flour was pretty old, may have been the problem...
I have made a similar called lazy wives pie but this was way better. I have made it twice now and the cast iron skillet makes a world of difference. Great recipe!
